items.title: Development of a Multimodal Large Language Model for Early Warning and Diagnosis of Dry Eye Disease
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background This study aimed to develop and externally validate an instruction-tuned multimodal large language model (MLLM) for early warning and early diagnosis of dry eye disease (DED) using routinely obtainable clinical data. Methods A total of 874 participants were enrolled, including an internal development cohort (n = 743) from Peking University Third Hospital (October 2024 to August 2025) and an independent external validation cohort (n = 131) from three additional centers. Participants included both DED and non-DED individuals, diagnosed according to the Chinese Expert Consensus (2020) and TFOS DEWS II criteria. We developed DED-MLLM on the basis of Qwen2-VL and constructed a domain-specific instruction-tuning dataset integrating Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), Standard Patient Evaluation of Eye Dryness (SPEED), self-reported questionnaires, ophthalmic imaging, and clinical examination data. Model performance was evaluated for risk stratification and diagnosis under both diagnostic frameworks, with ablation analyses used to examine the relative contributions of visual and structured clinical modalities. Results Based on the international diagnostic criteria for DED, the model achieved an accuracy of 0.8232 for early warning (specificity: 0.6873, sensitivity: 0.9558) and an accuracy of 0.9203 for diagnosis (specificity: 0.8776, sensitivity: 0.9720). According to the Chinese diagnostic criteria for DED, the model achieved an accuracy of 0.9584 for early warning (specificity: 0.9112, sensitivity: 0.9927) and an accuracy of 0.9327 for diagnosis (specificity: 0.8742, sensitivity: 0.9851). External validation showed AUCs of 0.910 and 0.957 for early warning and 0.960 and 0.893 for diagnosis. Ablation analyses indicated that structured clinical information contributed most strongly to diagnostic performance, whereas image-based information provided complementary, interpretable ocular-surface evidence. Conclusion The proposed DED-MLLM demonstrates excellent performance in both early warning and diagnosis of DED.

items.title: AmyloCore-ML: AI/Machine Learning Enabled Identification of Amyloid Fibril Core Regions Using Protein Language Models
items.abstract_or_text: Identification of amyloid forming regions in proteins remains central to understanding of their aggregation behaviour, which are central to various neurodegenerative and systemic disorders. Many predictors have been designed to identify amyloid forming regions, however they may not necessarily identify total residues found in actual disease associated fibril structures. To address this, we formed a sequence-based based predictor-AmyloCore-ML to ascertain structural amyloid-core propensity. The predictor was developed using experimentally determined fibril structures obtained from Amyloid Atlas. Ordered residues in the experimental structures were designated as core, and unresolved sampled from the same proteins as matched controls as non-core. Core and non-core regions were encoded using various physicochemical descriptors and protein language model (PLM) embeddings (ESM-2, ANKH, ProtT5) and evaluated using protein-grouped cross-validation. PLMs consistently outperformed physicochemical descriptors, with the best models reaching AUROC values of ~0.88 and AUPRC values of ~0.85. Locked full-length protein scans further localized experimental cores, with ESM-2/ExtraTrees achieving AUROC 0.833, AUPRC 0.751, and a mean peak distance of 12.4 residues. In comparative benchmarking, our predictor showed better performance metrics than CrossBeta and AggrescanAI. The framework therefore provides residue-resolved prediction of structurally incorporated amyloid-core regions directly from sequence.

items.title: Representing biological concepts as directions in foundation model embeddings
items.abstract_or_text: Biological foundation models encode rich information about protein structure, function, and cellular state in high-dimensional embeddings, but accessing specific biological properties typically relies on additional, task-specific prediction models. Here, we show that diverse biological properties can be mapped to interpretable, reusable directions in embedding space. In the Concept Activation Vector (CAV) approach, examples representing a concept are distinguished from a background set using a linear model, and the resulting weight vector defines the CAV for that concept. In protein embeddings, CAVs recover Gene Ontology and Enzyme Commission annotations, localize Pfam domains, reveal novel structural relationships, and capture DNA-binding and protein-interaction interface specificity. In single-cell embeddings, CAVs isolate cancer-associated expression transitions, and gene variation along these axes substantially agrees with conventional differential-expression analysis despite being a distinct computational approach. Together, these results establish concept directions as a common representation, enabling diverse biological features to be compared, localized, and manipulated.

items.title: Understanding when and how knowledge graphs add value to EHR-based clinical prediction across Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, and chronic pain
items.abstract_or_text: Biomedical knowledge graphs (KGs) have emerged as a promising approach for incorporating biological knowledge into machine-learning models trained on electronic health record (EHR) data. However, their large scale and heterogeneous structure impose substantial computational cost, and it remains unclear whether their benefits generalize across diseases or depend on how the graph is constructed. We systematically evaluated KG integration across three diseases spanning distinct biological and clinical characteristics: multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, and chronic pain. For each disease we compared five modelling strategies, spanning EHR-only features and graph diffusion over concept-level, cohort-derived, disease-anchored, and full SPOKE (Scalable Precision Medicine Open Knowledge Engine) subgraphs, asking whether graph construction affects predictive performance and computational cost, whether KG integration improves classification over EHR-only models, and what the graph does to model behavior. Cohort-derived subgraphs, comprising roughly 45% of SPOKE's nodes and one-fifth of its edges, matched or modestly exceeded the full graph's performance while substantially reducing computational cost in all three diseases. The predictive benefit of KG integration, however, was strongly disease-dependent: it improved classification in Parkinson's disease, had no measurable effect in multiple sclerosis, and reduced performance in chronic pain. These differences were not explained by the amount of biological information incorporated: the disease with the largest shift toward molecular features showed no improvement, the sole beneficiary showed only a modest shift, and the disease with no molecular shift was penalized. Mechanistically, graph diffusion redistributed each disease's existing signal across many correlated features rather than adding independent biological signal, so that any gain depended on whether it added information beyond the EHR. These findings show that cohort-derived subgraphs offer a computationally efficient alternative to full-scale knowledge graphs, and that KG integration functions less as a universal accuracy booster than as a data- and disease-dependent transformation of the patient representation.

items.title: Explainable Machine Learning-Based Diabetes Prediction Using Clinical Features: A Comparative Evaluation of Ensemble and Boosting Algorithms A Comparative Study with Explainable Artificial Intelligence Analysis
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder that requires early detection and effective management to reduce health complications. Machine learning approaches have demonstrated potential for identifying complex patterns in clinical data and improving disease prediction. This study presents a comparative analysis of multiple machine learning algorithms for diabetes prediction using clinical features. The Pima Indians Diabetes dataset containing 768 patient records and eight predictive variables was utilized in this study. Data preprocessing involved handling physiologically invalid zero values through median imputation. Five classification algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, optimized Random Forest, XGBoost, and optimized XGBoost, were developed and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC metrics. The optimized Random Forest achieved the highest overall accuracy of 76.62%, while Random Forest and optimized XGBoost demonstrated superior sensitivity for identifying diabetic cases. Furthermore, SHAP-based explainable artificial intelligence analysis revealed that glucose level, body mass index (BMI), and age were the most influential predictors contributing to model decisions. The findings highlight the potential of machine learning and explainable AI techniques for supporting diabetes risk prediction and clinical decision-support.

items.title: Microglia transcriptomic response to doxorubicin-induced genotoxic stress
items.abstract_or_text: Chemobrain, characterized by cognitive dysfunction, has emerged as a significant health concern following cancer treatment. Doxorubicin, an FDA-approved chemotherapeutic agent, is widely used to treat various cancers. However, its adverse effects raise concerns regarding toxicity in non-cancerous cell types. Microglia, the resident immune cells of the brain, play a central role in maintaining neural homeostasis. Despite this, the mechanisms by which microglia become dysfunctional following doxorubicin exposure remain poorly understood. Understanding the transcriptomic alterations induced by doxorubicin in microglia could provide critical insights into mechanisms underlying its neurotoxic effects. In this study, the transcriptomic response of human microglia to doxorubicin using mRNA sequencing combined with bioinformatic analysis was investigated. Exposure to doxorubicin significantly altered microglial morphology, promoting a shift toward a process-bearing phenotype in human HMC3 cells. This phenotypic change was accompanied by elevated levels of DNA damage and was associated with the induction of cellular senescence. At the gene regulation level, the Illumina-based transcriptomic analysis provided 25,834 gene expression profiling in which 5,669 were differentially expressed. The future analyses revealed that 3,431 (upregulated) and 2,238 (downregulated) were differentially expressed under the treatment of doxorubicin. Genes associated with the p53 signaling pathway and inflammatory responses were upregulated, whereas genes involved in translation, DNA replication, and cell-cycle progression were downregulated. This transcriptional dysregulation was accompanied by differential expression of key transcription factors. This study provides transcriptomic evidence elucidating the genotoxic response to doxorubicin in microglial cells, offering mechanistic insights into chemobrain and highlighting key molecular pathways as potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

items.title: Coordinated Enhancement of Molecular and Spatial Fidelity for Biological Inference in Spatial Transcriptomics
items.abstract_or_text: Understanding tissue organization requires accurate molecular quantification and faithful spatial localization. Spatial omics, particularly spatial transcriptomics (ST), face measurement trade-offs that limit simultaneous achievement of molecular and spatial fidelity across spatial resolution, detection sensitivity, molecular-tissue alignment and cell-level fidelity. Existing computational methods typically target individual aspects and optimize them in isolation, despite their interdependence. Here we present FOCUS, a multimodal generative foundation model for coordinated ST enhancement. FOCUS integrates native ST with histology images, cell masks, scRNA-seq references and spatial co-expression priors through task-specific modules, with cross-task coordination enabling joint correction of co-occurring limitations. FOCUS improved the performance of individual enhancement tasks and provided additional gains with coordinated mitigation of coupled limitations. Across immunology, tissue development and oncology, FOCUS recovered biologically consistent patterns obscured in native ST or isolated enhancement, enabling clearer inference of neutrophil-tumor interactions, spatial osteocyte differentiation and primary-metastatic HNSCC programs. Together, FOCUS establishes coordinated enhancement of molecular and spatial fidelity as a strategy for downstream biological inference from ST.

items.title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models reveals an advantage in the low-data regime for cell-type and disease-state prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Single-cell foundation models perform well on cell-type classification, but their value for disease-state prediction and their advantage over classical representations remains unclear. We benchmarked cell-representations from four foundation models using logistic regression, on 868 disease-prediction tasks (82 datasets) and 65 cell-type datasets from CELLxGENE. With full data, the baseline (log-normalized counts) outperformed the best model (TranscriptFormer-Sapiens) for cell type and matched it for disease. However, with few labeled cells, TranscriptFormer-Sapiens significantly outperformed the baseline in both tasks up to ~102 samples per class. Our comprehensive zero-shot benchmark identifies the data-scarce regime as a domain where Single-cell foundation models truly show advantage.

items.title: Concurrent de novo inference of cell types and gene regulatory networks with NetMap
items.abstract_or_text: Existing methods for GRN inference based on single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data typically require prior cell type calling and then infer GRNs at cell type resolution. This risks propagation of errors from cell annotation to GRN inference. Moreover, it makes existing methods blind to regulatory programs that are shared between different cell types, as well as to subtle differences in regulatory activity between cells of the same type. To address these limitations, we present NetMap, a pipeline that jointly infers cell-level GRNs and clusters cells based on shared regulatory programs, combining state-of-the-art single-cell autoencoders and explainable artificial intelligence methods. NetMap outperforms existing methods on synthetic data with a known ground-truth GRN and is able to reliably detect biologically plausible regulons on real data. Moreover, requiring only a small set of user-provided marker genes, NetMap can be used for GRN structure-informed probabilistic cell type assignment. We demonstrate the utility of this approach using PBMC data, where we achieve near perfect clustering and cell type recovery performance compared with manually created cell type labels. Finally, we applied NetMap to a data set with naive, activated and exhausted T-cells, and were able to verify that NetMap retrieves relevant T-cell state signatures from the data, with two approaches. NetMap can be installed as a python package from https://github.com/bionetslab/netmap and is compatible with the scverse system. Scripts to reproduce our results can be found at https://github.com/bionetslab/netmap-evaluation.

items.title: Taking the Harm out of Pharmaceuticals: An Analysis of Adverse Drug Reaction prevalence among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Purpose: To quantify adverse drug reactions (ADRs) requiring hospital admission among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples compared with Non-Indigenous Australians, and to assess whether disparities in ADRs exist across drug groups and age cohorts. Methods: : Retrospective population-based study using the AIHW National Hospital Morbidity Database (2006/07–2022/23). ADRs were identified using ICD-10-AM external cause codes Y40–Y59. Poisson regression with log population offsets estimated age-specific rates and rate ratios; negative binomial and Bayesian hierarchical models served as sensitivity analyses. Estimated marginal means were obtained using the emmeans package in R. Results are expressed as rate ratios with 95% highest posterior density (HPD) intervals. Results: : Of 3,192,098 ADR-related hospitalisations, 84,848 (2.7%) were among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. Eight drug groups showed consistently elevated rate ratios, with lower HPD bounds exceeding 1.0 in ≥60% of age-period combinations: antibiotics (Y40), hormones (Y42), blood constituent agents (Y44), antiepileptics (Y46), sedatives (Y47), antidepressants (Y49), cardiovascular drugs (Y52), and diuretics (Y54). Disparities were most pronounced in working-age adults, with rate ratios ranging from 1.5 to 3.77 in the 20–39 and 40–64 cohorts. Blood constituent agents in the 40–64 cohort recorded the highest rate ratio (RR 3.77; 95% HPD 3.55–4.00) in the most recent period. Absolute rate differences and rate ratios widened progressively across all four study periods for several drug groups. Conclusions: : Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples experience substantially higher rates of ADR-related hospitalisations than Non-Indigenous Australians, with disparities concentrated in working-age adults and widening over 18 years. These findings reflect exclusion from pharmacovigilance infrastructure, clinical trials, and pharmacogenomic research. Addressing them requires Indigenous-led pharmacovigilance reform, expanded medicines monitoring through community-controlled health organisations, and genuine inclusion of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples in pharmacogenomic research.

items.title: Construction and Validation of a Diagnostic Model for Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Based on Pyroptosis-Related Genes
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background: GERD is a common chronic digestive disorder, yet its diagnosis remains challenging due to the lack of objective molecular markers are lacking. Pyroptosis may contribute to esophageal mucosal injury, but a systematic search for pyroptosis-related diagnostic genes in GERD has not been performed. In this study, we used integrated bioinformatics, machine learning, and experimental validation to identify pyroptosis-associated diagnostic biomarkers for GERD and examine their relationship with the esophageal immune microenvironment. Methods: Esophageal transcriptome data from patients with GERD were obtained from the GEO database. We intersected differentially expressed genes, WGCNA module genes, and a curated set of pyroptosis-related genes to obtain candidate genes. We constructed a diagnostic model from 113 combinations of machine learning algorithms and validated it in an independent dataset using an artificial neural network. Immune cell infiltration was estimated with CIBERSORT, and the key bioinformatics results were further checked in a rat model of GERD. Results: The machine learning pipeline identified five pyroptosis-related genes with diagnostic value: GABARAPL1, CD55, CA9, SLC4A2, and LCN2. Among these, GABARAPL1 and CD55 performed best individually, with AUCs of 0.876 and 0.862. When the two genes were fed into an artificial neural network, the AUC reached 0.919 in the training cohort and 0.900 in the test cohort. Immune profiling showed that GERD esophageal mucosa contained more resting/activated dendritic cells, M2 macrophages, and activated NK cells, but fewer CD8⁺ T cells and γδ T cells. The animal experiments confirmed that GABARAPL1 was downregulated and CD55 was upregulated in GERD tissues. Conclusion: These observations point to GABARAPL1 and CD55 as potential pyroptosis-related diagnostic biomarkers for GERD. They may also influence disease pathogenesis through immunomodulatory mechanisms.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Imaging Technologies in Orthodontic Assessment, Referral and Care Pathways: A Scoping Review
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract* Background Artificial intelligence (AI), integrated with imaging technologies, is increasingly applied across orthodontic assessment and care pathways. However, the evidence remains scattered across imaging modalities, clinical applications, AI methodologies, and stages of clinical translation. Methods A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported in line with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore were searched for studies published between January 2016 and June 2026, with searches supplemented by Google Scholar, OpenAlex, grey literature sources, and citation searching. Eligible studies were mapped descriptively and synthesised thematically using Braun and Clarke’s framework. Results Fifty-four studies were included. AI applications used intraoral and facial photographs, cephalometric radiographs, CBCT, intraoral scans, three-dimensional dental models, and multimodal imaging. Applications ranged from landmark localisation, segmentation, and malocclusion classification to treatment-need assessment, screening, referral support, treatment planning, and remote monitoring. Evidence was strongest for bounded, anatomically verifiable image-analysis tasks, whereas applications involving referral, triage, treatment-need decisions, longitudinal prediction, and workflow integration were less mature. Common limitations included retrospective, single-centre designs; heterogeneous reference standards; limited external validation; inconsistent reporting of calibration and uncertainty; and insufficient evaluation of patient-centred, equity, and service-level outcomes. Conclusions Imaging-based AI in orthodontics has evolved from automated image interpretation to clinician-assisted decision support across the care pathway. Current evidence most strongly supports AI for structured image-analysis tasks, but does not yet support autonomous referral, triage, or treatment-planning decisions. Future research should prioritise prospective multicentre validation, transparent reporting, explainability, fairness, uncertainty handling, and workflow-integrated evaluation to enable safe and clinically useful implementation.

items.title: CRISCross: Integration of Epigenetic Information for Deep-Learning-Based Prediction of CRISPR-Cas9 Off-Targets Across Cell Types
items.abstract_or_text: CRISPR-Cas9 enables precise genome editing but remains limited by off-target effects, raising safety concerns and necessitating accurate prediction. Although epigenetic features influence Cas9 binding and cleavage, their predictive signals are often weak, highlyvariable, and context-dependent, limiting the effectiveness of existing machine learning approaches. Cross-cell-type settings are especially challenging: epigenetic landscapes differ substantially, and models trained on one cell type frequently fail to generalize. Here, we systematically investigate the role of epigenetic context in off-target prediction and demonstrate that its utility depends on modeling interactions with sequence features rather than treating it as an independent signal. Tabular and deep learning experiments demonstrate that epigenetic features provide a consistent but modestly complementary signal, and that late-stage fusion strategies are insufficient to effectively exploit this information. To address this, we introduce CRISCross, a cross-attention-based architecture that captures sequence-epigenetic interactions at the nucleotide level, alongside CRISPRAT, a synthetic pretraining strategy that learns transferable representations from genome-derived sgRNA-off-target pairs without relying on dataset-specific pretraining. CRISCross, incorporating AlphaGenome-derived chromatin accessibility signals, shows better predictive performance than sequence-only baselines across three independent test datasets spanning two cell types, demonstrating improved generalization across guide RNAs, datasets, and cellular contexts. This is particularly relevant for therapeutic applications involving cell types or patient-derived contexts that lack dedicated experimental datasets. In such settings, predicted chromatin accessibility may provide scalable contextual information when direct epigenomic profiling is unavailable or impractical. Together, these results show that accurate CRISPR off-target prediction benefits from interaction-aware integration of epigenetic context alongside generalizable pretraining strategies.

items.title: CHORUS: A proteome-scale atlas of membrane interaction interfaces constructed using cross-protein language model embeddings from sequences alone
items.abstract_or_text: Membrane proteins drive vital cellular signaling and bioenergetics yet resolving their physical interaction interfaces remains hindered by the paucity of experimental complexes and the breakdown of sequence alignments across hydrophobic bilayers. Here, we present CHORUS, a sequence-only deep-learning framework that decodes interaction sites across membrane proteins without requiring 3D structures, multiple sequence alignments (MSAs), or predefined partner identities. By systematically synthesizing complementary latent representations across diverse protein language model (pLM) families and functional layer depths, CHORUS outperforms 18 established sequence- and structure-based methods across 4,655 homology-isolated test contexts (average precision: 0.643), demonstrating amplified predictive capacity within the lipid-embedded core (0.746). We show that CHORUS delineates quaternary contact boundaries across megadalton respiratory supercomplexes directly from sequences alone (0.984). We deliver the CHORUS Atlas (https://chorus.atlas.sunnylab.org), providing precomputed, residue-resolved interaction landscapes for 80,619 reviewed transmembrane proteins spanning 4,918 species and 33.7 million residues to empower interactome-scale discovery and allosteric therapeutic design.

items.title: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Frontier and Local LLMs Querying a Biomedical Knowledge Graph
items.abstract_or_text: We combine GeneNetwork's 1TB structured database with its metadata as an RDF graph and an associated literature corpus. We benchmark frontier and local LLMs querying it through four architectures: document, graph and agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and a combination of the three. We evaluate them on 40 domain specific expert-curated questions with a new metric: the satisfaction frequency psi (psi, i.e, the share of questions answered with precision and recall of at least 70% or an f1 of at least 60%). psi ranks systems the same way precision, recall and f1 -- a machine learning metric built from the harmonic mean of precision and recall -- but is easier to read and assess for humans. System architecture had a large effect: with full use of Claude Opus 4.8 the plain document RAG of our earlier GNQA system had a psi of 36% against 86% for our new combined tools. Delegating most of the work from Claude Opus 4.8 to a local model halved query costs while still reaching a psi of 59%.

items.title: AMMPER-2: A spatially explicit agent-based model of microbial radiobiology with redox dye simulation
items.abstract_or_text: To reduce health risks for human space exploration, it is important to model the effects of deep-space radiation on biological systems. The budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a common model organism in space radiobiology, but little is known about how radiation damage to individual cells translates into the population-level effects that experiments measure. The Agent-Based Model for Microbial Populations Exposed to Radiation (AMMPER) is a spatially explicit agent-based model that simulates the effects of ionizing radiation on S. cerevisiae cells and produces population-level results. Its goal is to improve experiment design and data interpretation. AMMPER-1 demonstrated that agent-based simulations can qualitatively reproduce the effects of proton radiation on the growth rate of wild-type and DNA-repair mutant yeast. Here, we present AMMPER-2, which addresses limitations of the first model and expands its capabilities. AMMPER-2 incorporates the dynamics of the redox dye alamarBlue, a data type commonly generated in spaceflight microbiology experiments, and models the fate of reactive oxygen species in more detail. It also adds an improved graphical interface and runs faster. AMMPER-2 remains easy to execute in Python on a standard personal laptop, providing space biologists a tool to explore experimental conditions, generate hypotheses, and interpret data from microbial space radiation experiments.

items.title: A critical evaluation of Gene Ontology priors in biologically-informed neural networks
items.abstract_or_text: Biologically-informed neural networks (BINNs) embed prior knowledge such as the Gene Ontology (GO) into their architecture to produce interpretable representations, yet whether and how this prior improves performance or interpretation remains unclear. We introduce GONNECT, a BINN incorporating GO into an autoencoder. We evaluate GO constraints in the encoder, decoder, or both on RNA-seq tumour samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), comparing against published BINNs (OntoVAE, VEGA), an unconstrained baseline, randomized priors, and untrained networks. Across various performance metrics, GO structure adds little to reconstruction or latent-space organization, frequently matched by randomized or unconstrained models. Node activations agree with a gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA)-derived reference, but this agreement largely arises from the architectural constraint: it is lost when GO connections are randomized, present even before training in the encoder, and learned in the decoder. Regularized soft links outside GO (GONNECT-SL) are unstable across runs and concentrate where the ontology is sparse, compensating for the prior's constraints rather than revealing new biology. Within this setting, we find no evidence that node activations capture biological information beyond that encoded by the predefined gene sets, suggesting that their apparent interpretability largely reflects the prior imposed by the architecture.

items.title: AI-Driven Design of Next-Generation Immunoinformatics Multi-Epitope Subunit Vaccine Targeting the Most Virulent Mpox Proteome: A Structural and Kinetic Validation Framework
items.abstract_or_text: The resurgence of the Mpox virus (MPXV) highlights the urgent need for scalable, mutation-resistant countermeasures. Slow development timelines hinder traditional empirical vaccine discovery, while conventional vaccinology often yields high false-positive rates because it relies on static, linear sequence-based screening. These classical informatics filters consistently fail to predict physical structural stability or the dynamic presentation of immune cells under physiological conditions, creating a distinct translational gap between computational design and in vitro efficacy. To address these limitations, here we engineered an advanced, AI-augmented vaccine discovery pipeline targeting the most virulent components of the MPXV proteome. We systematically screened eight critical viral targets essential for replication, membrane morphogenesis, and host-cell entry to map highly conserved T-cell and B-cell epitopes. Moving beyond standard heuristic filtering, we implemented a high-fidelity deep learning validation layer: ESM-2 protein language models (pLMs) were deployed to calculate pseudo-perplexity scores across chimeric linker junctions (EAAAK, GPGPG) to guarantee structural naturalness, MHCflurry ensemble models successfully verified active intracellular antigen presentation, and structure-informed graph neural networks (GNNs) simulated the physical node-attention dynamics of the immune synapse. Finally, recurrent neural networks (RNNs)-driven mRNA kinetic modeling optimized translation initiation rates and minimum free energy profiles during in silico cloning. This multi-layered pipeline successfully yielded three structurally refined, multi-epitope vaccine constructs optimized for maximum global population coverage. ESM-2 structural validation confirmed exceptionally low perplexity scores at structural junctions, indicating that the engineered chimaeras have native-like stability and a minimized risk of proteolysis. GNN-based immune synapse modeling demonstrated highly stable binding kinetics and robust binding free energies between the target epitopes and human HLA alleles. Furthermore, RNN kinetic optimizations established that the cDNA sequences are optimized for high-yield expression in heterologous expression hosts without risk of ribosomal stalling or translational bottlenecks. This study establishes a deep learning-augmented framework that bridges the gap between theoretical sequence optimization and biopharmaceutical scalability. By validating the structural naturalness, real-world immunogenicity, and manufacturing kinetics of our vaccine chimeras, this framework presents a robust, proactive paradigm for rapid vaccine architecture against emerging orthopoxvirus threats.

items.title: Clinical utility of plasma APOE proteotyping for Alzheimer's disease risk and prognosis
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder strongly influenced by genetic factors, with apolipoprotein E (APOE) {epsilon}4 allele being the most established risk variant. Although DNA-based genotyping remains standard, plasma proteotyping may provide scalable, isoform-specific alternatives. Methods: Plasma APOE4 protein were quantified using the NULISAseq CNS panel across four cohorts (ADRC, HeartSCORE, LATTICE, and ALPS). DNA-based APOE genotyping was the reference standard. Proteotyping thresholds for APOE {epsilon}4 carrier status and copy number were derived in ADRC and externally validated in the other cohorts. Logistic, proportional-odds, and Cox proportional-hazards models compared genotype- and proteotype-defined groups in relation to amyloid positivity, cross-sectional CDR global scores, and time to CDR-SB worsening, respectively. Results: Plasma APOE4 accurately classified APOE {epsilon}4 carrier status in ADRC (AUC=0.977, 95%CI 0.967-0.985; threshold 5.78 NULISA protein quantification [NPQ] value) and achieved near-perfect external validation in HeartSCORE, LATTICE, and ALPS (all AUCs=1.000, 95%CI 1.000-1.000). Plasma APOE4 also well-differentiated heterozygous from homozygous {epsilon}4 carriers (ADRC AUC=0.879, 95%CI 0.834-0.921; threshold 12.23 NPQ value). Genotype- and proteotype-defined {epsilon}4 carrier status showed similar associations with amyloid positivity (OR=4.40 vs 4.45), higher CDR global scores (OR=1.50 for both), and CDR-SB worsening (HR=1.22 for both). Discussion: Plasma APOE4 proteotyping accurately distinguished genotype-defined APOE {epsilon}4 carrier status and copy number while demonstrating AD-related associations comparable to DNA genotyping.

items.title: Electronic Health Record-Based Machine Learning Models for Predicting Revascularization, Amputation, and Cardiovascular Mortality in At-Risk Patients
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and/or diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) are at increased risk for limb loss and death. Existing risk calculators lack consistent clinical adoption; therefore, we aimed to identify vascular and non-vascular predictors of revascularization, amputation, and cardiovascular death using data from the OMOP CDM plus vascular extension. We assembled a cohort of adults with PAD, CLTI, or DFU receiving care within the UNC Health System from 2014–2024 (n = 178,995). Using 127 vascular-specific and thousands of non-vascular HER variables, we used logistic regression with inverse probability weighting and MCMC-based dimensionality reduction to predict revascularization, amputation, and cardiovascular death. The mean age was 72.5 ± 13.9 years; 50.9% were female and 23.5% Black. The revascularization and amputation models performed well (AUC = 0.984 and 0.926, respectively), while cardiovascular mortality prediction was modest (AUC = 0.772). Revascularization predictors were dominated by arterial disease, amputation prediction was driven by treatment interactions with dementia and frailty, and cardiovascular events and risk factors were the strongest predictors of cardiovascular mortality. Prediction models derived from harmonized EHR data demonstrated strong performance for revascularization and amputation. These findings support harmonized EHR-based vascular prediction modeling and warrant multi-institutional validation.

items.title: Beyond the Final Layer: Evaluating Single-Cell Foundation Model Representations for Molecular Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Single-cell foundation models (scFMs) are commonly benchmarked using final-layer embeddings, although useful depth may depend on the task. We evaluate Geneformer, scBERT, scGPT, and scFoundation as frozen feature extractors for cell-type and perturbation-response prediction using layer-wise probes, leave-one-dataset-out (LODO) selection, readout controls, representation diagnostics, centered kernel alignment (CKA), and retrieval/collapse analyses. Intermediate layers significantly improve cell-type accuracy for scGPT and scBERT in several settings, while Geneformer and scFoundation generally show performance comparable to their final layers. For perturbation prediction, LODO identifies layer 1 as an earliest-on-par candidate across all four models, without establishing universal superiority. Paired scGPT CLS and mean-pooling analyses show that readout affects preferred depth. CKA and representation metrics reveal model- and task-dependent geometric changes, while retrieval and collapse checks support the robustness of perturbation findings. We recommend reporting extraction depth, readout, selection protocol, and task-specific diagnostics. A validated non-final layer may also reduce computation, although efficiency was not directly benchmarked.

items.title: A perturbation atlas of mouse neural organoids resolves macroglial reactivity and nominates drivers of degeneration
items.abstract_or_text: Understanding neuro-glial roles in homeostasis and disease requires scalable central nervous system (CNS) models, particularly as macroglia like astrocytes and Muller glia remain challenging to study in slow-developing human systems. Here, we generate and map the cellular diversity of mouse neural organoids spanning multiple brain regions and the retina. Benchmarking transcriptomic maturation against in vivo references captures postnatal neuro-macroglial states within a month. We show that macroglia are highly responsive to inflammatory cues and adopt specific transcriptomic states also found in vivo. Through a single-cell perturbation screen targeting 13 Muller-glia-specific pathways, we map how certain inflammatory cytokines drive degeneration-like stress programs in photoreceptors and distinct reactive states in Muller glia, including an Oncostatin M-driven chaperone-associated state. Mechanistically, we identify gp130-STAT3 signaling as a targetable driver of macroglial reactivity and photoreceptor distress. Together, these single-cell atlases provide a foundation for dissecting cellular crosstalk and neuro-glial pathology in the mature CNS.

items.title: Collapsing Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis Progression to ESRD Following Combination Therapy with Pembrolizumab and Enfortumab Vedotin: A Case Report
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Introduction: Pembrolizumab (PB), a PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibitor, and enfortumab vedotin (EV), a Nectin-4 targeting antibody-drug conjugate delivering the microtubule-disrupting payload MMAE, represent the current standard of care for advanced urothelial carcinoma. While PB-associated glomerulopathy is a recognized rare complication, rapid one-month progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD) following the EV-PB combination has not been previously described. Case Presentation: A 76-year-old male with high-grade urothelial carcinoma and baseline Stage 4 CKD (eGFR 25 mL/min/1.73 m^2, creatinine 2.5 mg/dL) secondary to prior cisplatin exposure was initiated on PB 200 mgIV and EV 1 mg/kg IV on a 21-day cycle. Within one month, he developed AKI presenting with a creatinine of 3.1 mg/dL, eGFR of 20 mL/min/1.73 m^2, and nephrotic-range proteinuria of 13.1 g/24 hours. Renal biopsy confirmed cFSGS with 53% global glomerulosclerosis and 70% cortical fibrosis. Both agents were discontinued, and rituximab was initiated; however, renal function still deteriorated. Six months later he presented with labs of: creatinine 8.4 mg/dL, eGFR 6 mL/min/1.73 m^2; requiring emergent hemodialysis. Renal function did not recover, and the patient progressed to permanent ESRD. Discussion/Conclusion: This case highlights three key teaching points. First, pre-existing CKD from prior nephrotoxic chemotherapy amplifies the risk of irreversible cFSGS progression following ADC-immunotherapy, underscoring the need for baseline nephrology evaluation in this population. Second, we propose a novel synergistic mechanism whereby PB-induced podocyte dedifferentiation and cell-cycle re-entry renders those podocytes selectively vulnerable to MMAE-mediated cytotoxicity which can potentially explain the unusually rapid deterioration observed. Third, once advanced interstitial fibrosis is established, immunosuppressive salvage is unlikely to alter the trajectory, and its toxicity must be weighed against a negligible probability of benefit. Notably, PB-induced cFSGS typically remits within 2–3 months of drug discontinuation; however, the literature on dual therapy with EV remains limited.

items.title: MESNet: A Lightweight Transformer-CNN Collaborative Network with Morphology Awareness for Glioma Segmentation
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Glioma segmentation is of great significance for clinical diagnosis and treatment, in which the effective utilization of multimodal information is crucial. Accurate segmentation holds substantial clinical value for guiding precise surgical resection, formulating personalized radiotherapy plans, and assessing prognosis. However, most existing methods focus primarily on the extraction and selection of deep semantic features while overlooking morphologically meaningful features such as edges and shapes. To address this issue, we propose a lightweight high-performance network named MESNet (Morphological Edge and Shape Network). MESNet is a Transformer–CNN collaborative segmentation model that explicitly imposes edge consistency and shape regularity to introduce morphological constraints, thereby enabling precise brain tumor segmentation. The model adopts an efficient 3D Transformer as its backbone, organically integrating convolutional neural networks to capture local details. Through deep complementarity between global context and fine-grained representations, it achieves accurate segmentation. To strengthen boundary awareness, a lightweight multi-scale edge-aware module is designed, which utilizes Sobel-based edge enhancement and spatial attention mechanisms to explicitly sharpen tumor boundaries, substantially reducing boundary errors without significantly increasing computational overhead. To accommodate irregular tumor morphology, an attention-guided shape-aware module is constructed; a zero-initialization strategy is employed to maintain training stability, and the module adaptively focuses on variations in tumor scale and shape, markedly improving the segmentation completeness and contour adherence of small targets such as enhancing tumors. Meanwhile, the network adheres to a lightweight design philosophy, strictly controlling parameter counts and computational complexity through channel compression and efficient attention mechanisms. Experimental results on the BraTS2021 dataset demonstrate that MESNet achieves overall segmentation accuracy and boundary agreement comparable to those of state-of-the-art methods while consuming substantially fewer resources, attaining a superior balance between efficiency and performance. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/tanjia123456/MESNet-main.

items.title: Dementia Language Models: a generalizable and controllable representation of cognitive impairment
items.abstract_or_text: We introduce Dementia Language Models (DeLMs)--generalizable and controllable representations of cognitive impairment through language--alongside an evaluation framework for establishing their validity and clinical grounding. DeLMs created by fine-tuning large language models on a small clinical corpus successfully generated patient-like narratives across unseen tasks, received predicted Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores in the impaired range, and produced narratives that neurologists identified with accuracy comparable to real transcripts. The models' internal representations, as well as their non-linguistic decision-making, supported mild cognitive impairment detection in unseen cohorts. The effect was controllable: moving from Healthy toward Dementia in weight space progressively worsened language and predicted MMSE scores while increasing dementia probability. DeLMs could support clinician training, hypothesis generation, and scalable experimentation, reserving patient involvement for where it is truly needed.

items.title: Intracellular accumulation of AAV6 genomes governs microglia reactivity and the inflammatory response in retinal gene therapy
items.abstract_or_text: Adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors possess immense potential for gene therapy applications. However, microglia can mount an immune response against AAV vectors. Yet, microglia are therapeutic targets since they play a driving role in the progression of neurodegenerative diseases. Thus, it is critical to understand the cellular processes driving the microglia-mediated immune response against AAV vectors. To this end, we modelled AAV6 induced inflammation upon retinal gene therapy in minipigs. Upon AAV6 administration, the IBA1+ cells demonstrated a morphological transition to the amoeboid form, indicating microglial reactivity. We also observed the invasion of peripheral immune cells in the retina. To elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, we transduced human iPSC derived microglia-like cells (iMGLs) in vitro with AAV6 and AAV8 respectively. Only AAV6 transduced iMGLs exhibited morphological features and a transcriptomic signature of microglial reactivity. The magnitude of intracellular AAV6 viral genomes was significantly higher as compared to the AAV8 condition. The elevated levels of intracellular AAV6 genomes induced a DNA damage response in AAV6-transduced iMGLs, which is a key feature of neuroinflammation-linked microglial reactivity. Thus, our work highlights the impact of intracellular viral genome accumulation on microglial reactivity and its implications for retinal gene therapy associated inflammation.

items.title: DNA methylation-based prediction of differentiation state at cell-type resolution reveals an age-associated epigenetic mesenchymal drift
items.abstract_or_text: Quantifying the differentiation state of cells is an important task in regenerative medicine, cellular reprogramming and in elucidating how differentiation hierarchies are altered in aging and disease. For DNA methylation data (DNAm) there is however an accute shortage of methods for quantifying differentiation state. Here we use machine learning to build EpiDiff, a predictor of differentiation that yields a continuous absolute differentiation index (DI) when applied to a DNAm sample. We extensively validate EpiDiff in single-cells, sorted cells and bulk tissue, as well as in in-vitro differentiation, organoid, reprogramming and cellular rejuvenation experiments. In mixed samples, EpiDiff measures the extent of differentiation across all cellular lineages. In sorted cell populations, we find that DI increases with age and, underpinning this increase, we discover that many cell-types undergo a developmental epigenetic drift that is most prominent towards the mesenchymal lineage. When applied to normal-tissues, EpiDiff is predictive of carcinogenic exposure and cancer risk. In summary, EpiDiff is a unique, general and versatile tool that can accurately quantify the global differentiation state of a DNAm sample with broad applicability to many disciplines.

items.title: Lineage tracing reveals asynchronous fate restriction in mouse embryos and stem cell-derived embryo models
items.abstract_or_text: How a flexible mammalian embryo gives rise to a reproducible body plan remains unclear, partly because cell lineages cannot be followed continuously in vivo. We combined DNA Typewriter lineage recording with tetraploid complementation to reconstruct high-resolution single-cell genealogies across mouse development and built FateVec, an analysis framework that infers fate-bias dynamics and lineage-associated transcriptional programs from reconstructed phylogenies. Loss of developmental potential proved progressive and asynchronous, with multiple lineages acquiring detectable fate bias before morphological diversification at gastrulation. Within the neural crest, most cells remained multipotent over an extended window, while independent founder clades differed markedly in restriction timing. Extending lineage recording to a stem-cell-derived embryo model revealed that cells with shared transcriptional identities can arise from distinct lineage relationships. We further found embryonic-lineage contributions to extraembryonic-like states, exposing an unexplored lineage plasticity. This lineage-resolved view of embryogenesis reveals that cell identity alone predicts neither developmental ancestry nor the timing of fate restriction.

items.title: Inherent limitations of zero-shot mutation prediction in protein engineering
items.abstract_or_text: Predicting mutation effects is critical for protein engineering. A commonly pursued strategy is zero-shot prediction with deep-learning models, whose performance is typically evaluated using aggregate benchmark scores that obscure multidimensional biological tradeoffs. Here, we evaluate sequence, structure, and hybrid foundation models across curated datasets to expose the practical limitations of zero-shot predictions. We demonstrate that model performance is highly variable and heavily influenced by experimental noise and competing phenotypic goals. Notably, predictions from competing models often correlate more strongly with one another than with experimental outcomes. While current models effectively filter deleterious mutations and enrich high-scoring variants for natural functions, they struggle to identify precise optimal mutations and consistently fail to predict mutations that drive new-to-nature functions. These models learn from evolutionary constraints that tend to oppose the extreme biophysical optimizations required in targeted engineering. Consequently, zero-shot scoring serves as a valuable initial filter but cannot substitute for task-specific prediction.

items.title: Linking somatic variants to altered methylation profiles in nanopore-derived breast and pancreatic cancer genomes using unduliner
items.abstract_or_text: Research shows that genetic variation directly influences DNA methylation, and this association has generally been explored on germline SNPs and at a population level. The presence of genomic variation and base modification on sequence reads generated from a technology like nanopore sequencing offers an opportunity to link disease-specific variants to methylation changes in individual genomes. Here, we present unduliner, a framework with an embedded pretrained convolutional neural network model, that predicts somatic variants, single-nucleotide (SNVs) and structural (SVs), associated with methylation pattern changes in cancer genomes. We trained the model (accuracy = 0.803 on validation; 0.897 on held-out test) using phased sequence reads, single-nucleotide germline variants, per-base methylation probability, and variant proximity or presence in haplotype-specific differentially methylated regions (DMRs). Unduliner was applied to subline-specific variants from MCF7 breast cancer cell lines as proof-of-concept, and we demonstrated its ability to identify variant-stratified methylation differences independent of haplotype-based methylation differences. In a pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) sample, we identified coding and non-coding SNVs and SVs associated with tumour-normal DMRs, allele-specific methylation, and intratumour DMRs. These observations demonstrate that integrating long-read methylation and variant information can provide additional interpretative context for both coding and non-coding genomic variation beyond the conventional variant impact prediction tools. The results from unduliner include variant information, size and direction of methylation change with respect to the variant (increase or decrease), and genomic location of methylation change. Unduliner is publicly available on GitHub at https://github.com/Chisomgold/unduliner.

items.title: Subtype-Selective Neuronal Vulnerability and Compensatory Neuroglial Remodeling in Human Cortical Dementia
items.abstract_or_text: Whether the nodal vulnerability in dementia is solely represented by changes in cellular abundance or attrition of cellular transcriptomic landscape attribute to that transition in aging brain is yet to uncover with minutiae. To understand this complication, we have analyzed two snRNA-seq data specific to (I) dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC): A comprehensive study of cellular profiling among cognitively normal and pathological ageing and dementia (AD) brain, (II) occipital cortex (OC) in the context of Nasu-Hakola disease along with a tissue level bulk RNA-seq data corresponds to temporal cortex. We pinpoint cellular subpopulations their proportional changes within the nodal points and their transcriptomic profiling. In DLPFC we observed alteration of mitochondrial and synaptic maintenance program in the pathological manifestation of disease. In OC we noticed depleted upper layer CUX2 neuron, PVALB and SST neurons on the contrary an enrichment of RORB and LAMP5 neurons with compromised metabolic states in the disease context. Glial populations are marked by representation of fibrous astrocyte, neuronal-supporting subpopulations associated with extracellular matrix remodeling programs. Proportional increment of intermediate myelinating oligodendrocyte and a decrease in mature myelinating subpopulation highlighted a compromised myelin repair attempt. In temporal cortex at tissue level we observed transcriptomic landscape adopted a neuroglial phenotypes in dementia brain. Cell-Chat analysis demonstrated a shift in cellular coordination towards glial population from neuron in NHD brain. A single cell-based drug reprofiling approach identified efatutazone and balaglitazone as broad-spectrum candidates for major cell types in occipital cortex, whereas major actionable biological targets belong to CDK subtypes and proteasome subunits. Overall, our findings imply cellular persistence do not necessarily substantiate molecular preservation, also the coexistence of cellular vulnerability alongside selective remodeling features, present a cellular framework on how to cope up with degenerative changes.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Tooth Numbering and Full-Mouth Series Placement
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract This study proposes an automated method for detecting tooth positions and predicting full-mouth series (FMS) radiograph placement using oriented object detection and Siamese neural networks. A total of 5,431 radiographs from 354 patients were annotated and used to train deep learning models. Oriented bounding boxes were generated using a YOLOv5 detector, followed by tooth numbering, feature extraction, and image classification via a multitask ResNet50 model. FMS placement was predicted using a Siamese neural network inspired by jigsaw-puzzle tasks, with permutation-based training and patient-level five-fold cross-validation. Mean tooth-numbering accuracy was 0.99 ± 0.00. Mean FMS-placement accuracy was 0.97 ± 0.01 for upper left and right periapical radiographs, 0.98 ± 0.02 for upper anterior periapical radiographs, 0.98 ± 0.01 for lower left and right periapical radiographs, 0.99 ± 0.01 for lower anterior periapical radiographs, and 0.96 ± 0.02 for bitewing radiographs; overall mean accuracy was 0.98 ± 0.01. This internally tested AI pipeline demonstrated high accuracy for tooth numbering and automated FMS arrangement and may help streamline dental radiographic workflows, subject to external and clinical validation.

items.title: Assessing User-Subjective Experience with Conversational Agents for Behavioral and Mental Health Interventions: Design and Psychometric Evaluation of CUE-Chat
items.abstract_or_text: While AI-conversational agents are increasingly integrated into behavioral and mental health interventions, standardized instruments to assess their performance remain scarce. To address this gap, we developed an instrument to measure user-subjective experience with AI-driven agents in the healthcare domain. We focused on user perception due to its direct contribution to intervention effects, and on healthcare given that the rapid adoption of AI-agents in this domain continues to outpace the development of validated evaluation instruments. Across four studies, we developed and tested the Chatbot User Evaluation instrument (CUE-Chat). First, we identified relevant assessment domains and items through literature review, existing instruments, input from AI-driven agents, and the research team’s domain expertise. Following this, we requested feedback on draft subscales, definitions, and items from expert and laypeople panels. We then tested the structure of the instrument’s concept version. Finally, we conducted a psychometric evaluation and finalized the instrument.CUE-Chat consists of four factors: Perceived Efficacy (4 items), Usability (4 items), Intelligence (4 items), and Safety and Risk Management (4 items). Reliability and validity of the total score and each subscale was good to excellent (Cronbach’s α = .73-.92; Ω = .74-.93). Predictive validity was strong with all scales predictive of users’ overall rating of an AI-agent’s performance.We conclude that CUE-Chat’s strong psychometric properties are promising, and that it is particularly useful for researchers integrating AI-driven agents into behavioral and mental health interventions in both developmental and evaluative stages.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Clinical, Laboratory, and Chest CT Features Between COVID-19 and H1N1 Pneumonia: A Large-Scale Retrospective Study with Machine Learning Integration
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Concurrent COVID-19 and influenza A(H1N1) epidemics since late 2019 have complicated early differentiation because of overlapping clinical and imaging features. Viral evolution, shifting population immunity, and emerging variants may have altered imaging phenotypes, underscoring the need for contemporary data. We aimed to compare clinical, laboratory, and CT characteristics between COVID-19 and H1N1 pneumonia, identify independent predictors for each diagnosis, and explore machine learning (ML) models for differentiation. Methods This retrospective study included 612 patients (442 H1N1, 170 COVID-19) diagnosed between January 2023 and December 2025. Clinical, laboratory, and chest CT features were comprehensively analyzed. Between-group differences were assessed by χ² test or Mann-Whitney U test. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify the independent predictive factors. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was used for feature selection. Five ML algorithms were trained (70% of cohort) and tested (30%). Model performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results Parenchymal involvement was more frequent in COVID-19 than in H1N1 pneumonia (91.2% vs 74.7%; P 0.001), with higher rates of ground‑glass opacities, interlobular septal thickening, and crazy-paving pattern. Airway involvement was more frequent in H1N1 pneumonia (48.2% vs 34.7%; P = 0.003), including higher rates of bronchial wall thickening, centrilobular nodules, and tree‑in‑bud nodules. On multivariable analysis, upper lobe involvement (OR = 2.19; 95% CI: 1.04, 4.65) and parenchymal involvement (OR = 3.44; 95% CI: 1.67, 7.10) were independent predictors of COVID-19. Tree-in-bud nodules (OR = 0.30; 95% CI: 0.12, 0.77), lymphadenopathy (OR = 0.29; 95% CI: 0.06, 0.81), and disorders of consciousness (OR = 0.20; 95% CI: 0.07, 0.61) were independently associated with H1N1 pneumonia. Among five ML models, the random forest model achieved the highest performance, with an AUC of 0.71 (95% CI: 0.58, 0.85) for differentiation. Conclusion Upper lobe involvement and parenchymal involvement are independent predictors of COVID-19, whereas tree-in-bud nodules, lymphadenopathy, and disorders of consciousness are independently associated with H1N1 pneumonia. These imaging and clinical features may facilitate early differential diagnosis.

items.title: Probable neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease in an Asian woman without detectable NOTCH2NLC repeat expansion on routine testing
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background: Neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease (NIID) is a clinically heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder characterized by eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions. GGC repeat expansion in NOTCH2NLC is strongly associated with adult-onset NIID in East Asian populations. Fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome (FXTAS), associated with an FMR1 CGG premutation, can overlap with NIID clinically, radiologically, and pathologically. Negative targeted repeat-expansion results therefore require interpretation alongside clinicopathological findings. Case presentation: A 67-year-old Asian woman with no known family history of neurological disease developed progressive cognitive decline in 2021, followed by limb ataxia and bilateral lower-limb weakness. In 2025, her ADL and mRS scores were 51/56 and 3; MoCA and MMSE scores were 8/30 and 19/30. Electrophysiological findings suggested predominantly motor demyelinating polyneuropathy. Brain MRI showed bilateral corticomedullary-junction hyperintensities on DWI and confluent periventricular and deep white-matter abnormalities on FLAIR and T2WI. A skin biopsy obtained above the lateral malleolus showed eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions in sweat gland epithelial cells and fibroblasts, with positive SQSTM1/p62 and SUMO1 immunostaining. RP-PCR did not detect a NOTCH2NLC GGC repeat expansion. Both FMR1 alleles were reported to contain 29 CGG repeats, below the premutation range. During 14 months of follow-up, no impaired consciousness, seizures, or encephalopathy-like episodes occurred, and the mRS Scale score remained 3. Cognitive scores changed in opposite directions, precluding conclusions about cognitive change or treatment response. The clinical, radiological, and previously reported pathological findings supported probable NIID, apparently sporadic, without molecular confirmation. Conclusions: Characteristic MRI and skin biopsy findings remain diagnostically informative when routine NOTCH2NLC screening detects no expansion. FMR1 analysis aids differentiation from FXTAS. A negative targeted result alone should neither exclude NIID nor imply a novel causative gene; confirmation using an independent repeat-expansion assay or long-read sequencing should be considered when available.

items.title: Multimodal Glymphatic Imaging in Multiple Sclerosis: Associations with Sleep and Disability
items.abstract_or_text: The glymphatic system is the waste clearance pathway in the central nervous system. Although its dysfunction has been associated with several neurological disorders, its role in multiple sclerosis (MS) remains poorly understood. This system is thought to be particularly active during sleep, yet the relationship between sleep metrics and MRI-derived markers of glymphatic activity has been scarcely explored. In this study, we aimed to perform a multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) assessment of glymphatic function in MS and investigate its association with sleep parameters, clinical disability, disease duration and MRI-derived structural markers. The study included 22 patients (34.3{+/-}10.1 years; 16 female) with relapsing-remitting MS and 26 healthy controls (32.2{+/-}5.7 years; 18 female), all of whom underwent 3.0 Tesla MRI. Glymphatic function was assessed using diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index and global blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) signal-cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) coupling. In addition, sleep micro- and macrostructural features, clinical disability, disease duration, along with mean diffusivity (MD), lateral ventricular, choroid plexus volumes and lesion load were evaluated. Patients showed reduced DTI-ALPS index, though this difference became only a trend after controlling for MD. No significant group differences were observed in global BOLD signal-CSF coupling. However, in patients, the weaker coupling was associated with longer total sleep time, lower arousal index, greater disability and lateral ventricle enlargement, whereas the DTI-ALPS index showed no significant correlations with any of the measures. Together, these findings challenge the assumption that DTI-ALPS can serve as a reliable marker of glymphatic function in demyelinating diseases such as MS, where disease-related alterations in white matter microstructure can confound diffusion-based measures. In contrast, gBOLD-CSF coupling showed associations with sleep, clinical disability and structural changes in patients, despite the absence of a significant group-level difference. This finding suggests that gBOLD-CSF coupling may capture individual variability in glymphatic-related dynamics relevant to sleep and the clinical expression of MS.

items.title: Cell Painting and machine learning for mechanistic profiling of hepatotoxic botanicals and their constituents
items.abstract_or_text: BACKGROUND Botanicals are widely consumed as herbal remedies and plant-derived products, but their complex and variable chemical composition presents major challenges for safety assessment. Although hepatotoxicity has been reported for several botanicals, the constituent compounds responsible and the underlying mechanisms often remain poorly characterised. OBJECTIVES We aimed to determine whether Cell Painting could identify candidate constituent drivers of botanical bioactivity and generate hypotheses about potential mechanisms of action in primary human hepatocytes. METHODS We profiled 13 botanical extracts and 85 known constituents across multiple concentrations using Cell Painting alongside assays of metabolic activity and membrane integrity. To interpret morphological phenotypes, we trained machine-learning models using a Cell Painting reference atlas of >1,000 chemicals linked to ToxCast/Tox21 molecular and cellular bioactivity annotations. RESULTS Cell Painting detected bioactivity in 11/13 botanical extracts and 46/85 constituents, compared with 9/13 extracts and 40/85 constituents in the cell-health assays, and generally detected activity at lower concentrations. For 9/13 extracts, at least one constituent was active at a lower concentration than the corresponding botanical extract, supporting the contribution of a subset of potent constituents to mixture-level responses. Aristolochia and goldenseal were the most potent extracts across Cell Painting and cell-health assays and contained highly active constituents. Reference-atlas models generated specific mechanistic hypotheses, including cytotoxicity-, endocrine-, and genotoxicity-associated responses for several botanicals and constituents. CONCLUSION These results support Cell Painting combined with machine learning as a sensitive approach for characterising cellular responses to botanicals, prioritising candidate constituent drivers of hepatotoxicity-associated phenotypes, and generating testable hypotheses about potential mechanisms of action.

items.title: Probing Physical Intuition in Large Language Models through Partner-Dependent Mutation Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Structure-guided mutation design requires relating a proposed substitution to its molecular environment to anticipate its effects. Existing evaluations of large language models (LLMs) in protein engineering emphasize sequence-based prediction or tool-integrated workflows, leaving unclear whether LLMs themselves can infer mutation effects from structural evidence without dedicated predictors. We evaluate physical intuition-qualitative reasoning that connects structural observations with molecular interaction principles-using a benchmark that tests the same substitution in the same protein across different binding partners, with predictions based on local atomic coordinates and no dedicated mutation-effect predictors. In the tested comparisons, the best-performing LLM achieved group accuracy comparable to the evaluated energy predictors and Biomni, an LLM-driven tool workflow, while the methods differed in their prediction patterns. Most evaluated LLMs achieved higher group accuracy for larger affinity improvements. Structural interventions support selective dependence on mutation-site and partner information, while assessable structural claims largely agree with the supplied coordinates. These findings support direct LLM structural reasoning as a basis for developing rational mutation-design tools that connect molecular observations with partner-specific effects.

items.title: tRNAZAP: Deep learning toolkit for nanopore tRNA signal analysis
items.abstract_or_text: tRNA are short, ~76 nucleotide-long, modification-rich molecules that play an important role in protein translation. Nanopore sequencing is the only platform capable of directly sequencing full-length, native tRNA molecules. This capability is enabled by splinted ligation of tRNA-specific adapters. As a result, the measured ionic current signal reflects a composition of both adapter and tRNA sequence features. Despite these advantages, analysis of nanopore tRNA sequencing data poses distinct computational challenges. Existing ionic current-based signal-to-sequence decoding (basecalling) models are optimized for mRNA and perform suboptimally on short, modification-dense RNA such as tRNA. Furthermore, alignment algorithms for reference-guided analysis of short-length reads are not optimized for nanopore reads with lower accuracy than Next-generation sequencing reads. To overcome these limitations, domain-specific computational approaches are required. We present tRNAZAP, a nanopore ionic current signal analysis toolkit designed to enable precise reference-guided sequence alignment. tRNAZAP operates directly on raw ionic current signals and decomposes the analysis into two complementary tasks: 1) segmentation of adapter and tRNA regions, and 2) tRNA classification, both implemented using transformer-based models. The segmentation component isolates the tRNA signal portion and extracts the corresponding nucleotide sequence as the alignment query, while the classification component identifies the tRNA type as the alignment reference without requiring sequence-level information. Together, these outputs allow direct optimal pairwise alignment between the tRNA subsequence of the full query and reference sequences. Trained on in vitro transcribed RNA data and evaluated on yeast tRNA, these models achieved ~98% classification accuracy and intersection-over-union of ~0.98 for segmentation.

items.title: 5-HT1A Antagonist WAY-100635 Prevents Chronic Neurodegeneration and Immune Activation After TBI
items.abstract_or_text: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) initiates secondary neurodegeneration that compromises interconnected neural circuits and contributes to persistent visual and neurobehavioral impairment. Pharmacological strategies that preserve vulnerable neurons and synapses while limiting chronic neuroinflammation remain an unmet therapeutic need. We previously identified the serotonin 1A receptor (5-HT1A) antagonist WAY-100635 through screening human stem cell-derived retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and demonstrated that it promotes neuroprotection through cyclic adenosine monophosphate-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis. Here, we investigated whether post-injury treatment extends this neuroprotective efficacy to cerebral and visual circuitry following TBI. Male C57BL/6J mice aged 2-3 months underwent unilateral controlled cortical impact (CCI) involving the left visual cortex. Mice were randomly assigned to sham, untreated injury or treated injury groups, with 3-10 sham controls and 5-8 mice per injury group across experiments. WAY-100635 was administered intraperitoneally at 5 mg/kg daily, beginning 1 hour after injury and continuing for 6 weeks. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed using motor and psychological-health-relevant risk-taking/behavioral disinhibition by elevated-plus-maze assessment, visual electrophysiology, optokinetic responses, diffusion magnetic resonance imaging, and retinal and cortical histopathology. Unilateral cortical injury produced bilateral RGC dysfunction and loss, with greater degeneration in the eye contralateral to the injured hemisphere, consistent with predominantly crossed murine visual projections. WAY-100635 significantly preserved RGC survival and function, improved visual acuity and contrast sensitivity, and preserved visually evoked cortical responses to contralateral eye stimulation. Diffusion MRI revealed bilateral visual pathway abnormalities, with treatment selectively normalizing fractional anisotropy and radial kurtosis in the optic tract ipsilateral to cortical injury. In perilesional cortex, treatment preserved neuronal cell bodies and synapses detected by synaptophysin immunoreactivity while markedly reducing microglial/macrophage activation and reactive astrogliosis. These effects were accompanied by improved early motor performance and attenuation of injury-associated increases in open-arm exploration in the elevated plus maze. Cortical cavity volume was not significantly reduced, supporting preferential protection of vulnerable circuitry surrounding and connected to the primary lesion. These findings identify post-injury WAY-100635 treatment as a novel therapeutic intervention that combines neuronal and synaptic preservation with reduced chronic glial activation and improved functional outcomes. They support further translational development of serotonin 1A receptor antagonism to limit secondary neurodegeneration and the visual and neurobehavioral consequences of TBI.

items.title: AnnZarro: scalable, interactive exploration of cell-by-cell and gene-by-gene relationships in single-cell data
items.abstract_or_text: Cell-by-cell and gene-by-gene relationships, such as kernels and correlations, shape most single-cell analyses but are rarely inspected directly due to a lack of visualization tools that display them. AnnZarro is a point-and-click browser viewer that shows these matrices linked to an AnnData object's cells x genes data. Using AnnZarro, experimental biologists can explore data without code and computational biologists can probe the relationships behind their analyses. One focused cell and one focused gene drive every panel. Clicking a cell paints its row of any cell-by-cell matrix over an embedding or spatial coordinates; clicking a gene paints its row of any gene-by-gene matrix over a gene plot such as a volcano. The focus also links genes to the cells where they change, and cells to the genes that distinguish them. AnnZarro reads only the matrix rows and columns each panel displays from zarr stores and hence users can explore matrices far larger than memory on a laptop or a shared server. Large datasets open on a reproducible subset, and users step through the remaining cells in parts. On a laptop, a 100,000-cell part of Tahoe-100M opens in 4 s and stays interactive. With the subset switched off, AnnZarro draws all 95.6 million cells in one plot in about 5 to 7 s. This tutorial prepares a dataset with Kompot differential abundance and expression, a diffusion kernel and gene correlations, then explores it in six worked examples.

items.title: WHITE-Net : White matter HyperIntensities Tissue Extraction using deep learning Network
items.abstract_or_text: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are a hallmark of cerebral small vessel disease, a highly prevalent condition in aging, making their accurate detection in large-scale magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies critically important. Currently available semi-automated and automated segmentation methods are frequently limited by sensitivity to variations in imaging conditions and computational constraints, restricting their applicability across diverse acquisition settings. We present WHITE-Net, a deep learning-based framework for automated WMH segmentation built on a 3D ResUNet architecture and trained on multisite MRI data encompassing substantial variability in scanner vendors, acquisition protocols, spatial resolution, and image characteristics. Evaluated across three independent datasets - BrainLaus, ADNI, and WMH Challenge, WHITE-Net achieves high segmentation accuracy and ranks among the top-performing methods across datasets, enabling a comprehensive assessment of generalisability in varied imaging environments. WHITE-Net maintains stable performance in a wide spectrum of lesion loads and demonstrates a favorable balance between precision and recall, effectively limiting false positive detections - a common limitation of existing approaches. Beyond accuracy, WHITE-Net requires no parameter tuning and offers fast inference times, making it well-suited for deployment in large-scale neuroimaging studies. The obtained results highlight the value of training on diverse multisite data for improving generalisability and position WHITE-Net as a reliable, scalable tool for automated WMH segmentation in computational anatomy research.

items.title: From APTs to advanced persistent biological threats (APBTs): a taxonomy and large-scale metadata audit of genomic surveillance infrastructure
items.abstract_or_text: Open genomic repositories have become critical infrastructure for pathogen surveillance, variant tracking, outbreak reconstruction, and public health decision making. However, many of these repositories were designed to support rapid scientific data sharing rather than adversarial verification, creating potential security gaps. This paper introduces Advanced Persistent Biological Threats (APBTs), as a framework for understanding how malicious cyber biological actors can gradually disrupt genomic surveillance without entering a laboratory or releasing a biological agent. Instead of altering biological material, an attacker targets the sequence data, metadata, reference datasets, and analytical models used by surveillance systems.
