We present, to our knowledge, the first integrated multilayer taxonomy of APBTs, structured around a four phase lifecycle, and investigate whether the metadata weaknesses identified by this framework are present in an operational genomic repository. To assess this, we audited 100,000 SARS-CoV-2 BioSample records obtained from the NCBI. A framework of 23 checks was applied across five metadata layers: temporal, geographic, host and specimen, provenance, and technical metadata. Every record triggered at least one APBT relevant metadata vulnerability indicator, with a mean of 7.34 indicators per record (SD = 1.34). Overall, 97.3% of records were classified in the High or Critical severity categories. Every record also contained at least one indicator in both the provenance and technical metadata layers. These results largely reflect the optional status of several fields in the current BioSample submission model rather than isolated errors by individual data contributors. Temporal and geographic information was comparatively complete, while fields needed for provenance reconstruction, chain of custody assessment, technical validation, and analytical interpretation were frequently missing. These findings do not indicate deliberate manipulation. However, the structural incompleteness of BioSample metadata creates vulnerabilities that an adversary can exploit to introduce poisoned, misleading, or weakly traceable metadata into genomic repositories. As a result, maliciously altered metadata can appear plausible, remain undetected, and influence downstream genomic analysis and surveillance. The findings therefore show that widely used pathogen genomic repositories already contain structural weaknesses that can support metadata poisoning as part of an APBT operation.

items.title: AI-guided discovery for low-resource peptide engineering using evolutionary scale modeling
items.abstract_or_text: Data scarcity is a major bottleneck in artificial intelligence (AI)-guided peptide engineering, where experimental training sets often contain only tens to a few hundred sequences, and it is difficult to judge in advance whether a protein language model (PLM) will effectively guide iterative discovery before committing to wet-lab work. Here we present SCARSE, a machine learning framework that couples ESM2 protein language model embeddings with Gaussian process regression. Benchmarked across 24 diverse peptide and small-protein datasets spanning substitution and indel variants, antimicrobial peptides, and hemolytic peptides, SCARSE significantly outperformed hand-engineered descriptor baselines on substitution and indel tasks in low-data regimes (20-500 training samples) and performed comparably on short non-mutant peptides. In active learning simulations it consistently prioritized high-performing candidates, discovering up to 7-fold more top-tier peptides than random sampling. Cross-validation (CV) R2 correlated strongly with final active learning performance (Pearson r = 0.80-0.84), and evaluating on as few as 50 labeled peptides reduced CV R2 variance enough for it to serve as a practical, data-efficient criterion for assessing model suitability before iterative screening. SCARSE thus provides an early diagnostic indicator for active learning success and is freely available as an open-source Python package (pip) and through an interactive Hugging Face Spaces web interface.

items.title: EEG Pathology Detection via Clinical Concept Bottleneck Models
items.abstract_or_text: Deep learning models for electroencephalography (EEG) pathology detection achieve competitive accuracy but offer limited interpretability. In this paper, we introduce concept bottleneck models (CBMs) for EEG pathology detection which use clinical EEG biomarkers computed analytically from the signal as a bottleneck to be used for prediction. Those concepts include band power, spectral ratios, alpha peak frequency and amplitude, hemispheric asymmetry and phase locking values. With the backbone based on shallow convolutional neural network (CNN), we compare a black box baseline with two variants of CBMs. The hybrid variant is a classifier receives a residual projection of the backbone features. The pure variant is a CBM where the classifier receives only the predicted concepts. Models are evaluated on abnormality detection and dementia classification followed by concept prediction quality and leakage analysis. Both CBMs approach the baseline on TUAB (82.7-82.9% vs 83.6%) and are 2-5 percentage points lower on CAUEEG (57.9-60.5% vs 62.7%). The pure CBM exhibits concept fidelity concern where the predicted concepts deviate from their ground truth values. Replacing them with their true values causes severe cost on accuracy by 26 and 22 points on TUAB and CAUEEG. The concept fidelity concern is mitigated by increasing the weight of the concept loss to match the ground truth concepts. the mitigation comes with small accuracy cost on TUAB but a relatively larger cost on CAUEEG. The code of the experiments and full logs are available at https://www.github.com/mhmdrdwn/cbm.

items.title: Data-efficient machine learning for the detection of duodenal neoplasia: a multi-centre study
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Machine Learning (ML) has shown promise in histopathological diagnosis, but rare tumours, like duodenal epithelial neoplasms, are challenging because large, labelled datasets are difficult to assemble. We propose a data-efficient ML pipeline for detecting duodenal epithelial neoplasia in whole-slide images. Methods: We assembled a five-hospital dataset of haematoxylin and eosin-stained duodenal biopsy whole slide images (WSIs) at 10x magnification, comprising 8,027 normal and 401 neoplastic biopsies, including adenomas, carcinomas and neuroendocrine tumours. WSIs were divided into patches and encoded using the Hibou-B foundation model. We compared global standardisation with unsupervised site-specific standardisation of patch embeddings. Our pipeline combined principal component analysis, a Gaussian mixture model and a Random Forest classifier. We assessed generalisability using leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation across four hospitals and on an independent test set from a fifth hospital. Results: In leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation, the pipeline achieved a mean accuracy of 90%, sensitivity of 96%, specificity of 83% and an AUC of 0.96. On the external test hospital, it achieved 94% accuracy, 93% sensitivity, 95% specificity, and AUC of 0.97. Site-specific standardisation improved mean cross-validation accuracy by 20 percentage points compared with global standardisation, while the Gaussian mixture pipeline improved accuracy by 12 percentage points compared with mean pooling of patch embeddings. Conclusions: We present a data-efficient ML approach for detecting duodenal epithelial neoplasia from WSIs. Strong performance was maintained across hospitals and on an independent external test cohort despite the limited number of neoplastic training cases, supporting the feasibility of foundation-model-based approaches for rare histopathological diagnoses.

items.title: AI-Assisted Tissue-Based Antibody Interpretation in Autoimmune Encephalitis: Prospective Validation and Reader Study
items.abstract_or_text: Tissue-based assays provide broad screening for neural autoantibodies but remain vulnerable to technical and reader-dependent variability. We evaluated an integrated workflow combining automated 3,3'-diaminobenzidine tissue-based assay processing, digital whole-slide imaging, and interpretable deep learning. Model development used 2,357 retrospective serum and cerebrospinal fluid images referred from more than 80 institutions and processed in a centralized laboratory, with reference labels established by expert-consensus tissue-based assay interpretation. A prospective validation cohort included 200 images from 200 unique patients (154 positive and 46 negative; 100 serum and 100 cerebrospinal fluid). The same images were evaluated by two expert and two novice readers in a fixed-order two-round study, with unaided interpretation followed by artificial-intelligence-assisted interpretation after a washout of at least two weeks. The standalone binary classifier achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.922, accuracy of 86.5%, sensitivity of 85.7%, and specificity of 89.1% in prospective validation. Pooled reader accuracy was 90.4% in the unaided round and 97.4% in the artificial-intelligence-assisted round (McNemar P < 0.001), with specificity of 82.6% and 99.5%, respectively. Novice-reader accuracy was 83.3% unaided and 96.5% with artificial-intelligence assistance (P < 0.001), approaching unaided expert accuracy of 97.5%. Among tissue-based-assay-positive cases, reader accuracy for cytoplasmic/nuclear antigen-associated versus neural surface antigen-associated staining-pattern subclassification was 88.8% unaided and 94.0% with artificial-intelligence assistance (P < 0.001). These findings support further multicentre, cross-platform evaluation of artificial-intelligence-assisted neural autoantibody tissue interpretation.

items.title: From examinations to consultations: a physician-reviewed Japanese benchmark for large language models in traditional Kampo medicine
items.abstract_or_text: Objectives: Patients and clinicians increasingly ask large language models (LLMs) about Kampo, Japan's traditional medicine. Yet evaluations of LLMs have measured accuracy on examination questions, which ask what a model knows; a consultation asks whether it can apply that knowledge to the patient at hand. No benchmark had measured that. Materials and Methods: KampoBench comprises 74 consultation scenarios and 310 conversation-specific rubric criteria, following the design of HealthBench. Scenarios, criteria and reference answers were drafted by an LLM and revised by board-certified Kampo physicians. Ten current models from three vendors were evaluated. Because LLM graders are known to favor their own family, each response was graded by a model from each vendor. Results: The best model reached 74.8-86.3% across graders, the physician-revised reference answers 87.9-92.4%. Rankings were stable across graders (Spearman's rho 0.952-0.976), and the family-favoring deviation was 0.4 to 0.6 percentage points, below the bootstrap standard deviation of one measurement; grader leniency varied by 14.3 points. Models were most reliable on criteria about advising that care be sought (83.6%) and least reliable on those requiring a known crude-drug risk to be tied to the case (17.5%), though 79.2% of those responses named the drug. Discussion: The shortfall lay in applying knowledge to the case rather than in holding it - a distinction examination-format evaluations cannot make. Conclusion: Evaluation in traditional medicine should measure the judgments a consultation requires, not recall alone. Quoted alongside the grader that produced it, a KampoBench score is a usable measure of those judgments.

items.title: A Systematic Literature Review of Machine Learning-Based Person and Scene Analysis Using Eye-Reflected Images
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Among the various reflective imaging modalities, eye reflections have emerged as a valuable source of visual information for person and scene analysis. Such imagery can capture contextual and identity-related cues from reflected environments, supporting applications in forensic analysis, biometric recognition, intelligent surveillance, and safety-critical domains. However, analysis of persons and scenes using eye-reflected images remains challenging due to their inherently small spatial extent, optical distortions, motion blur, illumination variability, and limited image resolution. Although machine learning techniques have demonstrated potential in addressing these challenges, existing research remains fragmented across different tasks, approaches, and application domains. While substantial research has investigated face identification and computer vision tasks using direct images, no systematic review has comprehensively synthesised machine learning-based approaches for person and scene analysis using eye-reflected images. This study addresses this gap by critically analysing machine learning techniques for person and scene analysis using eye-reflected images. A total of 12 primary studies, published between January 2006 and August 2026, were systematically identified and selected from Q1 and Q2 journals. The systematic review was conducted in accordance with the guidelines proposed by Kitchenham and Charters and the PRISMA 2020 framework. The review examined eye-reflected image sources, datasets, preprocessing techniques, machine learning models and architectures, analysis tasks, evaluation metrics, and application domains. A taxonomy of machine learning-based person and scene analysis is proposed to organise and synthesise this research area. The review identifies key research gaps and limitations and outlines future research directions to advance person and scene analysis using eye-reflected images.

items.title: Machine Learning and Logistic Regression Models Incorporating Clinical and CT-Derived Muscle-Fat Parameters for Predicting Geriatric Hip Fracture: A Prospective Study
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Hip fractures cause substantial morbidity and mortality in older adults. Sarcopenia is a key modifiable risk factor, yet few models integrate CT-derived muscle-fat metrics with clinical data. This study aimed to develop a risk prediction model for elderly hip fractures, compare multiple machine learning algorithms, and convert the optimal model into an interpretable nomogram. This prospective cohort enrolled patients aged ≥ 60 years undergoing hip CT, including fracture cases and controls. Muscle/fat area, mean attenuation, and skeletal muscle index were measured at femoral head, lesser trochanter, and L3. The cohort was split 7:3 into training and validation sets. Eight classifiers were built using Boruta-selected features, with performance assessed by AUC, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The logistic regression (LR) achieved the highest AUC (0.779). Multivariable regression retained eight independent predictors: age, elevated glucose, osteoporosis, fat area1/2, muscle mean2, SMI1, and SMI3. The nomogram incorporating these variables showed good discrimination (training AUC = 0.826; validation AUC = 0.817), favorable calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.647 and 0.412, respectively), and clinical net benefit on DCA. LR performed comparably or better than other ML algorithms. The nomogram offers a simple, interpretable tool for individualized hip fracture risk stratification using eight routinely available parameters.

items.title: Harmine derivative ACB1801 induces ferroptosis vulnerability and STAT1 pathway activation to sensitize MSS colorectal cancer to anti–PD-1 immunotherapy
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Harmine and its derivatives, a class of β-carboline alkaloids, are promising natural antitumor agents with drug resistance–modulating activities. Emerging evidence suggests that these small molecules can reshape the tumor microenvironment (TME) and modulate antitumor immunity. Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapies provide durable benefit in a subset of colorectal cancers but remain largely ineffective in microsatellite-stable (MSS) subtype, which accounts for approximately 85% of cases. This lack of response is driven by an immune-desert TME characterized by defective antigen presentation and poor cytotoxic T cell infiltration. Whether harmine derivatives can enhance ICB efficacy in MSS colorectal cancer remains unknown, and the underlying molecular mechanisms are poorly defined. We therefore evaluated how ACB1801, a synthetic derivative of the natural harmine, reprograms the TME to restore sensitivity to anti-Programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) therapy in MSS CRC. In murine MSS CRC models, ACB1801 markedly enhanced the antitumor efficacy of anti–PD-1, resulting in increased intratumoral CD8⁺ T cell infiltration and reduced regulatory T cell accumulation. Integrated transcriptomic analyses of sorted CD45⁺ immune and CD45⁻ tumor compartments revealed that combination therapy induced coordinated metabolic reprogramming, characterized by suppression of glycolysis and activation of ferroptosis-related pathways. These findings were validated in murine and human MSS CRC cell lines, where ACB1801 reduced glycolytic flux and increased ferroptotic susceptibility. Mechanistically, ACB1801 enhanced C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 10 (CXCL10) secretion in a STAT1-dependent manner and upregulated NOD-like receptor family CARD domain containing 5 (NLRC5)-driven MHC class I antigen presentation, thereby increasing tumor immunogenicity. Together, these effects convert immunologically “cold” MSS tumors into an immune-responsive state. Collectively, our findings position ACB1801 as a clinically relevant metabolic-immunomodulatory agent and provide strong preclinical justification for combining harmine derivatives with anti–PD-1 therapy to overcome resistance in MSS CRC patients.

items.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Hill Grading of Gastroesophageal Flap Valve: Model Development and Correlation Validation Against High-Resolution Esophageal Manometry
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Objective To develop an artificial intelligence (AI) model based on ResNet and Hill classification of gastroesophageal flap valve (GEFV) for endoscopic diagnosis of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and reduce the subjectivity of manual grading, and provide decision support for clinical GERD risk stratification and anti-reflux therapy selection. Methods In this single-center retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 7,652 endoscopic images from patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) were split into training, validation, and test sets at a patient-level 7:2:1 ratio. A ResNet-152 model was trained with class-weighted cross-entropy loss. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, and F1-score. Correlation with mean lower esophageal sphincter (LES) pressure from high-resolution manometry (HRM) was assessed in an independent cohort of 92 patients. Results Inter-observer agreement among expert endoscopists yielded a weighted Kappa of 0.73. The final model achieved an overall test-set accuracy of 85.02%, with per-grade accuracies of 84.76%, 80.95%, 76.19%, and 72.38% for Hill grades I–IV, respectively. items.title: Insights Into an Antibacterial Type VI Membrane-Disrupting Effector Of Adherent Invasive Escherichia coli
items.abstract_or_text: Adherent Invasive Escherichia coli (AIEC) strains are associated with ileal Crohn's disease and may contribute to intestinal dysbiosis through antibacterial competition. The AIEC reference strain LF82 encodes two type VI secretion systems (T6SSs), a contractile machine that injects an effector-loaded needle made of Hcp, VgrG and PAAR into neighbouring rivals, favoring niche colonization. LF82 T6SSs harbour several putative antibacterial toxin-immunity modules. Here we characterize the T6SS-1 encoded Tme AIEC , a PAAR-fused T6SS effector carrying a C-terminal Tme domain, hallmark of Tme (Type VI membrane disrupting effector) toxins, and its DUF1240-like immunity protein Tmi AIEC . When heterologously produced in E. coli K-12 as well as in E. coli and Citrobacter clinical isolates, Tme AIEC is toxic only upon periplasmic targeting, and its toxicity is neutralized by Tmi AIEC . Periplasmically-targeted Tme AIEC inserts into the inner membrane, collapses the proton motive force and increases cell permeability, consistent with a membrane-disrupting activity. Mutational analyses coupled to functional assays identified a predicted hydrophobic transmembrane segment and a conserved aspartate residue within the Tme domain as key determinants for Tme AIEC toxicity. These findings establish Tme AIEC /Tmi AIEC as a functional T6SS toxin-immunity pair and reveal conserved determinants underlying the activity of Tme-family membrane-disrupting effectors.

items.title: UniMedSeg: Unified Multi-Modal Medical Image Segmentation via Uncertainty Guided Encoding and Frequency-Spatial Dual-Prompt Decoding
items.abstract_or_text: Text-driven medical image segmentation demands unified models based on multi-modal learning, capable of processing diverse imaging modalities while providing spatially reliable prediction estimates for clinical practice. Nevertheless, existing vision-language model solutions suffer from poor domain generalization and exhibit limited capability for uncertainty estimation to model the cumulative unreliability of cross-modal alignment across network layers. In this paper, we propose UniMedSeg, a unified vision-language framework for multi-modal medical image segmentation built upon frozen pre-trained vision-language backbones. Our framework incorporates modality-aware adaptation, cross-layer uncertainty-guided encoding, and a frequency-spatial dual-prompt decoder, wherein the progressive uncertainty propagation mechanism of the encoder suppresses misleading cross-modal features, whereas the decoder disentangles anatomical structure and boundary details in the frequency domain under dual textual prompts. Auxiliary losses further sharpen boundary representations and calibrate pixel-wise uncertainty maps. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UniMedSeg preserves competitive in-domain segmentation performance, improves domain generalization, and yields clinically useful spatial risk estimation.

items.title: A Zero-Shot Decision Model (Jev) Matches a Trained Classifier but Ranks Its Own Errors Worse: Calibrated, Split-Conformal Next-Procedure Recommendation in General Dentistry
items.abstract_or_text: On real-world dental records, procedure history predicts the next procedure category well, and a simple history-aware classical model beats every large-language-model (LLM) design we tested. We study the question that follows every dental diagnosis: given a patients chart and most recent procedure, what should the dentist do next? Commercial dental artificial intelligence in 2026 is overwhelmingly diagnostic, and the closest published system for this sequencing task, MultiTP (Chen et al., 2024b), offers neither calibrated uncertainty, structured rationale, nor an evaluation as decision support. We introduce DentaCoPilot, a recommender that returns a calibrated top-K distribution over Current Dental Terminology (CDT) codes, a verbalised confidence label, an explicit abstain flag, and a chart-grounded rationale, and we compare four classical baselines with six LLM variants. On an apples-to-apples synthetic evaluation, classical baselines reach 0.567 top-1 while pure LLM variants trail at 0.267 to 0.467, and moving the backbone from Sonnet to Opus does not help. Prompt-conditioning a Sonnet LLM on the classical baselines candidate list closes most of the gap while preserving rationale and abstention; because the synthetic generator shares Markov structure with the bigram baseline, these synthetic rankings index pipeline behaviour, not externally valid clinical performance. We anchor external validity for the task on the public MEPS 2023 corpus (11,016 next-visit transitions across 5,088 patients): a history-aware model reaches 0.479 top-1 against 0.297 for a most-frequent baseline, is well calibrated (expected calibration error 0.031), and supports split-conformal selective prediction with a distribution-free coverage guarantee. A zero-shot LLM given only 1 this coarse history loses to the same classical baseline, so the LLMs value depends on rich charts rather than category history alone. Prospective clinician-in-the-loop validation and CDT-level real-data validation remain future work, contingent on clinical-data access and ethics approval that we have sought but not secured.

items.title: High-throughput variant libraries and machine learning enable robust target-site selection for toehold-switch design in Detectrons
items.abstract_or_text: Programmable RNA sensors enable sequence-specific detection of RNA inputs for diagnostics, genetic circuit control, and multiplexed molecular readouts. Although readily programmable, their performance varies substantially with the target site selected within a transcript, making target-site selection a major challenge. Here, we report DeSTAR (Detectron Sensor TARget-site ranker), a machine-learning-assisted target-site ranking model for programmable RNA sensors. To train this model, we generated transcript-wide, single-nucleotide-resolution tiling sensor libraries across six diverse RNA targets, enabling generalization to be tested across transcripts rather than within a single RNA. In leave-one-transcript-out evaluation, DeSTAR's top-ranked sites were enriched for high-performing sensors in held-out transcripts, driven predominantly by interpretable sequence grammar in the sensor stem rather than transcript-specific patterns. Prospectively, on an unseen SARS-CoV-2 transcript, the model's top-ranked sites yielded working sensors roughly five-fold more often than random selection. These results support DeSTAR as a generalizable strategy for target-site selection in RNA sensors across transcripts.

items.title: EvSpark: Lossless Speculative Decoding for Hybrid DNA Foundation Models
items.abstract_or_text: Hybrid DNA foundation models combine convolutional, recurrent, and attention layers, making speculative decoding more difficult than truncating a KV cache. We present EvSpark, a speculative decoding system for Evo2 that verifies draft blocks in parallel and restores all three classes of inference state by selecting retained intermediate states, without replay. A compact, hidden-state-conditioned drafter proposes each block in one parallel forward pass. On Evo2 7B, a 48-prompt benchmark with three training seeds yields a 2.96-fold speedup on 43 real-sequence prompts and a 3.27-fold speedup including five synthetic controls. Acceleration persists at 262k-token context (1.84-2.43-fold speedup on two bacterial genomes) and over 32k generated tokens. Retraining the same drafter architecture for Evo2 20B and 40B yields 2.18-2.46-fold speedups on real sequences and 2.51-2.78-fold speedups on the full suite. Autoregressive drafter comparisons and batch measurements show why low draft latency, rather than acceptance alone, determines the gain. The method preserves the target distribution. Greedy checks find no non-tie divergences across 48 prompts and six checkpoints; complementary sampling diagnostics quantify decoding fidelity. A drafter trained on 30M supervised positions reaches a 2.82-fold speedup on real sequences, compared with a 2.96-fold speedup at 150M positions. In regulatory-DNA design, EvSpark achieves a median 1.57-fold complete-workflow speedup over a calibrated batched native baseline.

items.title: Large language models differ in patient education quality across the robot-assisted radical prostatectomy care pathway
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Patients considering robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) require information that spans diagnosis, treatment selection, functional recovery, and recurrence surveillance. We compared the quality of English-language RARP patient education generated by ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Doubao. Twenty-five questions covering screening, diagnosis, treatment decision-making, perioperative care, rehabilitation, and follow-up were submitted individually to each model, yielding 75 responses. Three blinded clinicians evaluated the responses using the Global Quality Score, modified DISCERN, Quality Analysis of Medical Artificial Intelligence, Ensuring Quality Information for Patients, and the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool; six readability indices were also calculated. Overall Global Quality Scores did not differ significantly across models. ChatGPT achieved a higher EQIP score (median, 75.00%) than DeepSeek and Doubao (65.83% each) and greater PEMAT actionability (59.00% vs. 54.33% and 47.67%, respectively). DeepSeek generated comparatively easier-to-read text, although all three models exceeded commonly recommended sixth- to eighth-grade reading levels for public-facing health materials. Under the majority-rater criterion, no factual errors or outdated recommendations were identified, whereas key omissions occurred mainly in DeepSeek and Doubao responses. Inter-rater agreement was low, indicating substantial uncertainty in multidimensional human assessment. LLMs may support the preparation of clinician-reviewed RARP educational materials but should not replace individualized counseling by urologists.

items.title: Evaluation of Iodine-Based Contrast Agents for Ex Vivo Micro-CT Imaging of Porcine Hearts: An Application to Cardiac Conduction System Imaging
items.abstract_or_text: Purpose: This study compares two iodine-based contrast agents, iodine in ethanol (I2E) and aqueous solution of potassium triiodide (I2KI), in optimizing high-resolution, contrast-enhanced micro computed tomography imaging (micro-CT) of the cardiac conduction system (CCS) in porcine hearts. The study evaluates their relative efficacy in enhancing tissue contrast and anatomical delineation, aiming to improve CCS visualization for advanced cardiac research. Methods: Dissected porcine hearts were stained with I2E or I2KI for contrast enhancement and scanned with micro-computed tomography. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and volumetric shrinkage were evaluated. Additionally, qualitative visualization of CCS-related anatomical landmarks, such as the sinoatrial node (SAN), atrioventricular node (AVN), and Purkinje fibres, was performed, along with assessment of artefact occurrence and sample integrity. The efficacy of the contrast agents was also determined by segmenting the regions of interest corresponding to the CCS from micro-CT images. These were then further validated against histology. Results: I2E provided superior CNR, fewer artefacts, and preserved sample integrity, enabling smooth post-processing and histological sectioning. I2KI staining produced higher soft-tissue signal intensity and faster stain saturation (day 2) than I2E (day 3). However, I2KI exhibited leaching and introduced substantial staining artefacts. I2KI also exhibited structural disintegration, which, in turn, compromised downstream processing. Conclusion: These results suggest that I2E is a viable alternative to I2KI for CCS micro-CT imaging when sample preservation and downstream analyses are essential, whereas I2KI may be preferred for rapid, high-intensity staining where tissue integrity is less critical.

items.title: Deep Learning Trained Without Target-Domain Labels Improves Risk Stratification Over Expert Coronary Calcium Reading on Routine Attenuation Correction CT
items.abstract_or_text: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) is an established measure of coronary atherosclerosis on computed tomography (CT). Many SPECT and most PET myocardial perfusion studies already include a low-dose CT scan from which coronary calcium could be reported, yet it almost never is. CAC may not be reported due to image noise, cardiac motion, or the absence of a reliable reference standard. Deep learning (DL) models trained on these low-dose CT scans inherit the same uncertainty, because their reference labels are drawn on the degraded images. We bypassed this limitation by training a DL CAC model entirely outside the target domain: expert labels from high-quality gated CT were inherited by synthetic ungated images derived from those same scans, so that no CTAC scan was annotated, and no real CTAC image was used, at any point in training. Models were trained using one center and externally tested in two other centers. Because each synthetic image is derived from the gated scan itself, expert gated segmentations remain valid voxel-for-voxel without registration. Using these pairs, we developed a cross-domain knowledge adaptation model (knowledge adaptation, KAD-CAC). The DL models were externally tested on 5969 patients with a median age of 64 (IQR 56 - 73), of whom 50.2% were male. The KAD-CAC model had higher Cohens kappa K (0.86, 95% CI 0.84 - 0.88) compared to a convolutional LSTM model (K 0.78, 95% CI 0.76 - 0.80, p<0.01), or models trained with only gated images (K 0.81, 95% CI 0.80 - 0.82, p<0.01). Net reclassification improvement for death or myocardial infarction over a clinical and perfusion baseline was greatest for the KAD-CAC model and exceeded that of expert CAC reading on the same CTAC scans (difference 0.089, 95% CI 0.051 to 0.125, p<0.001). A model trained without any labels from CTAC scans therefore stratified risk of death or MI better than expert reading of the same scans. Patients classified as CAC 0 by KAD-CAC had lower adjusted risk of death or MI than patients classified as CAC 0 by experts (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.25 - 0.98). We use paired synthetic ungated scans to transfer expert gated CAC annotations into the ungated domain, resulting in better vessel-level CAC scoring and improved risk reclassification compared with expert reading of the same scans. Automated CAC scoring could be added to every myocardial perfusion imaging report without additional imaging or radiation. The approach provides a general route to expert-quality supervision for any acquisition in which the native reference standard is unreliable.
